presidentialSuccession.name: Manuel Zelaya
presidentialSuccession.notes: Ousted in June 2009 coup; later founded LIBRE.

supremeCourt.name: Corte Suprema de Justicia
supremeCourt.appointmentMethod: Magistrates elected by the National Congress for 7-year terms.
supremeCourt.fspEraChanges: Before the FSP era: in Dec 2012 Congress removed four Constitutional Chamber justices ("technical coup"), and in 2015 the court lifted the ban on presidential re-election (enabling Hernández). Under Castro/LIBRE, Congress elected a new 15-magistrate court in Feb 2023.
supremeCourt.stillServing: The 15-magistrate court elected by Congress in Feb 2023 (under LIBRE) is current; its partisan balance reflects the multi-party negotiation in Congress.

courtHistory.event: Through the 'banana republic' era and the military governments (1960s–80s) the court was weak; the 1982 Constitution set the current 15-magistrate court elected by Congress.
During the coup against President Zelaya, the Supreme Court ordered his arrest — pivotal, as Zelaya later founded the FSP-member party LIBRE.
In December Congress summarily removed four Constitutional Chamber justices (a 'technical coup') after rulings against the government.
The Supreme Court struck down the ban on presidential re-election, enabling Juan Orlando Hernández's 2017 re-election.
Under the Castro/LIBRE government, Congress elected a new 15-magistrate court in February after a multi-party negotiation.

supremeCourt.justicesNote: The 15-magistrate CSJ elected in 2023 is current; individual members are not itemized here.
